intro.title: What does Exyconn build for travel and tourism businesses?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that draft itineraries, prepare quotes, collect travel documents and look after travellers during the trip, so your consultants spend their time selling and fixing the hard problems. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents for travel agencies, tour operators and DMCs, on top of the booking engine, supplier contracts, CRM and mid-office you already use. A consultant signs off every quote before it goes out.

benefits.title: Why travel businesses are doing this now

items.text: Most enquiries now start on WhatsApp, and the first agency to send a sensible plan usually wins the booking.
A custom itinerary can take a consultant hours to put together from supplier rates and notes.
Travellers abroad need help at hours when your office in India is closed.
Visa rules and document lists change often, and one missing paper can sink a trip.
Package margins are thin, so knowing which supplier and which trip actually make money matters.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a travel agency's hours actually go
props.lede: Talk to any agency owner and the work that wears the team down is rarely the selling.

items.title: Enquiries that go cold
items.text: Leads arrive from WhatsApp, Instagram, the website and referrals. Many are price-shoppers, but the good ones get lost in the pile if nobody replies the same day.

items.title: Itineraries built by hand
items.text: A consultant copies hotel descriptions, rates and day plans from supplier sheets into a document, then redoes it when the client changes one city.

items.title: Calls from abroad at 2am
items.text: A missed transfer in Bangkok or a lost hotel voucher in Dubai lands on the owner's personal phone, because there is nobody else awake to answer.

items.title: Chasing passports and papers
items.text: Passport copies, photos, bank statements and forms arrive in pieces over email and WhatsApp. Someone has to check each one against the embassy's list.

items.title: Schedule changes found too late
items.text: Airlines retime and cancel flights, and the agency often hears about it from the traveller. Connecting transfers and hotel check-ins then need fixing in a rush.

items.title: Margins worked out after the trip
items.text: Supplier invoices, refunds and currency moves are reconciled weeks later, so nobody knows which package or supplier actually earned money until the season is over.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your consultants' desks

items.title: Trip planning and itineraries
items.text: Asks the traveller the right questions, then drafts a day-by-day itinerary from your own packages, preferred hotels and supplier contracts, in your agency's template.

items.title: Quotes and bookings
items.text: Prices the itinerary from your contracted and live supplier rates, applies your markup, and prepares the quote for a consultant to approve. Once accepted, it books through your booking engine and sends vouchers.

items.title: Traveller support, day and night
items.text: Answers travellers on WhatsApp during the trip from their booking: pickup times, hotel addresses, what's included. Anything that needs a decision goes to the on-call consultant with the booking attached.

items.title: Visa and document checklists
items.text: Sends each traveller the checklist for their destination and nationality, collects scans on WhatsApp, checks passport validity and blank pages, and flags missing items before the appointment.

items.title: Disruption alerts
items.text: Watches flight schedule changes on booked PNRs, tells the traveller and the consultant straight away, and drafts the knock-on changes to transfers and hotel check-ins.

items.title: Supplier and margin reports
items.text: Matches supplier invoices and refunds against bookings in the mid-office and reports margin by trip, destination and supplier, with outstanding payables listed.

props.lede: A Wednesday in peak booking season for an agency selling outbound holidays from India. Each moment lights the part of the business the agent is working on.

moments.title: A flight retimed overnight
moments.text: A Singapore flight for a family of four has moved by three hours. The family and their consultant get a message before breakfast, with the airport transfer already re-requested.

moments.title: Overnight enquiries, already drafted
moments.text: Eleven enquiries came in overnight. Each has a draft itinerary waiting from the agency's own Kerala, Dubai and Bali packages, sorted by how ready the traveller is to book.

moments.title: A quote goes out
moments.text: A consultant reviews a seven-night Switzerland quote the agent priced from contracted hotel rates, adjusts one hotel and sends it. The client accepts by evening.

moments.title: A missing bank statement caught
moments.text: A group of six is applying for Schengen visas. The agent notices one traveller sent only three months of statements and asks for the rest before the appointment date.

moments.title: Supplier payments, lined up
moments.text: The owner gets margin by trip for last month's departures and a list of supplier payments due this week, with one hotel invoice that doesn't match the booking.

moments.title: A traveller needs help in Bali
moments.text: A couple can't find their driver at Denpasar airport. The agent sends the driver's name and number from the voucher and alerts the on-call consultant while they wait.

items.question: Will this replace my travel consultants?
items.answer: No. It does the first draft and the follow-up work: replying, pulling rates together, chasing documents and sending updates. Consultants still approve every quote, handle tricky changes and build the relationship that brings clients back.

items.question: Can it connect to our booking engine and suppliers?
items.answer: It works with booking engines, GDS-connected tools, CRMs and mid-office systems that have an API or a reliable export, and with supplier rate sheets you already keep. In the first week we confirm what your stack allows the agent to read and book.

items.question: Does the agent decide on visas?
items.answer: No. It sends the published checklist for the destination, collects and checks documents for completeness and flags gaps. The embassy or consulate decides on the visa, and your team gives any advice beyond the checklist.

items.question: What about passport and payment data?
items.answer: Passport scans and traveller details are stored in your systems or a private environment we set up for you, with role-based access and an audit log. The setup follows the privacy law that applies, such as India's DPDP Act or the GDPR for European travellers, and card payments go through your payment gateway, never the chat.

items.question: What if something goes wrong at 3am?
items.answer: The agent answers what it can from the booking straight away. If the traveller is stuck, unsafe or needs money spent, it calls in your on-call consultant with the booking and conversation attached, and keeps the traveller updated until someone takes over.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on enquiry volume, the channels you use and which systems need connecting. Most agencies start with enquiries and itineraries; tell us about your business and we'll send a fixed quote for that first phase.
